title: 6.7 A 10b Source-Driver IC with All-Channel Automatic Offset Calibration and Slew-Rate-Enhanced Amplifier Achieving 2273pm2/Channel and 1.9mV DVO for 6285-PPI OLED-on-Silicon Displays
problem: Microdisplays for AR/VR (4K×4K, >120Hz refresh) require compact, high-pixel-density source-driver ICs; OLED-on-Silicon (OLEDoS) integrates pixel/driving circuits on silicon but demands tight area budgets (2273pm²/ch) and low display voltage offset (DVO) for color fidelity.
motivation: AR/VR user immersion depends on high resolution (4K×4K, >120 PPD), compact form factor, and high refresh (>120Hz); OLEDoS promises high integration but requires innovative driver design for area efficiency and signal fidelity.
method: 10-bit source-driver IC with all-channel automatic offset calibration and slew-rate-enhanced amplifier on OLEDoS backplane; achieves 2273pm²/channel area and 1.9mV DVO for 6285 PPI display through integrated low-area calibration and fast-slew output stage.
key_novelty: First OLEDoS source driver achieving sub-pJ-energy area footprint (2273pm²/ch) with automatic per-channel calibration, enabling high-resolution (6285 PPI) AR/VR microdisplays without external trimming overhead.
contributions: All-channel automatic offset calibration eliminating external trimming
Slew-rate-enhanced amplifier for rapid pixel-switching and refresh rates >120Hz
Ultra-compact area: 2273 pm²/channel on OLEDoS backplane
Low display voltage offset (1.9 mV) for accurate color reproduction at 6285 PPI
baselines: Prior OLEDoS source drivers, traditional TFT-based display drivers
limitations: Power consumption, detailed calibration precision, and comparison with competing high-PPI source-driver solutions not provided; temperature stability and aging performance not discussed.
primary_theme: Compact automatic-calibration source driver for ultra-high-PPI OLEDoS
